metadata.expected_sql: SELECT * FROM products WHERE price > 50

results.test_name: simple_count: How many customers do we have?...

metadata.expected_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customers

metadata.expected_sql: SELECT * FROM orders ORDER BY order_date DESC

results.test_name: simple_limit: Show me the 10 most expensive products...

metadata.expected_sql: SELECT * FROM products ORDER BY price DESC LIMIT 10

results.test_name: inner_join: Show me all orders with customer names...

metadata.expected_sql: SELECT o.*, c.name AS customer_name FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.id

results.test_name: left_join: Show all customers and their orders, includin...

metadata.expected_sql: SELECT c.*, o.id AS order_id, o.total FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON c.id = o.customer_id

results.test_name: join_filter: Which customers bought products in the Electr...

metadata.expected_sql: SELECT DISTINCT c.name FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.id WHERE p.category = 'Electronics'

results.test_name: join_count: How many orders does each customer have?...

metadata.expected_sql: SELECT c.name, COUNT(o.id) AS order_count FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON c.id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.name

results.test_name: self_join: Find pairs of products in the same category...

metadata.expected_sql: SELECT p1.name AS product_1, p2.name AS product_2, p1.category FROM products p1 JOIN products p2 ON p1.category = p2.category AND p1.id < p2.id

results.test_name: aggregation: What is the total revenue by product category...

metadata.expected_sql: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_revenue FROM order_items oi JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.id GROUP BY p.category

results.test_name: having: Which categories have more than 100 orders?...

metadata.expected_sql: SELECT p.category, COUNT(DISTINCT o.id) AS order_count FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON o.id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.id GROUP BY p.category HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT o.id) > 100

results.test_name: multi_agg: Show me the average, minimum, and maximum ord...

metadata.expected_sql: SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month', order_date) AS month, AVG(total) AS avg_total, MIN(total) AS min_total, MAX(total) AS max_total FROM orders GROUP BY DATE_TRUNC('month', order_date) ORDER BY month

results.test_name: percentage: What percentage of total revenue does each ca...

metadata.expected_sql: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS category_revenue, ROUND(SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) * 100.0 / (SELECT SUM(quantity * unit_price) FROM order_items), 2) AS revenue_percentage FROM order_items oi JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.id GROUP BY p.category ORDER BY category_revenue DESC

results.test_name: conditional_agg: Count how many orders are above and below ave...

metadata.expected_sql: SELECT CASE WHEN total > (SELECT AVG(total) FROM orders) THEN 'Above Average' ELSE 'Below Average' END AS category, COUNT(*) AS order_count FROM orders GROUP BY CASE WHEN total > (SELECT AVG(total) FROM orders) THEN 'Above Average' ELSE 'Below Average' END

results.test_name: cte: Show me the running total of monthly revenue...

metadata.expected_sql: WITH monthly_revenue AS (SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month', o.order_date) AS month, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS revenue FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON o.id = oi.order_id GROUP BY DATE_TRUNC('month', o.order_date)) SELECT month, revenue, SUM(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY month) AS running_total FROM monthly_revenue ORDER BY month

results.test_name: window_rank: Rank customers by total spending and show top...

metadata.expected_sql: WITH customer_spending AS (SELECT c.id, c.name, SUM(o.total) AS total_spent, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY SUM(o.total) DESC) AS spending_rank FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.id, c.name) SELECT name, total_spent, spending_rank FROM customer_spending WHERE spending_rank <= 5

results.test_name: lag_lead: Show month-over-month revenue growth percenta...

metadata.expected_sql: WITH monthly AS (SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month', order_date) AS month, SUM(total) AS revenue FROM orders GROUP BY DATE_TRUNC('month', order_date)) SELECT month, revenue, LAG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY month) AS prev_revenue, ROUND((revenue - LAG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY month)) * 100.0 / LAG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY month), 2) AS growth_pct FROM monthly ORDER BY month

results.test_name: correlated_subquery: Find products that are priced above the avera...

metadata.expected_sql: SELECT p.name, p.price, p.category FROM products p WHERE p.price > (SELECT AVG(p2.price) FROM products p2 WHERE p2.category = p.category)

results.test_name: multi_cte: Show customer segments: classify customers as...

metadata.expected_sql: WITH customer_totals AS (SELECT c.id, c.name, SUM(o.total) AS total_spent FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.id, c.name), stats AS (SELECT AVG(total_spent) AS avg_spent, STDDEV(total_spent) AS std_spent FROM customer_totals) SELECT ct.name, ct.total_spent, CASE WHEN ct.total_spent > s.avg_spent + s.std_spent THEN 'High Value' WHEN ct.total_spent > s.avg_spent - s.std_spent THEN 'Medium Value' ELSE 'Low Value' END AS segment FROM customer_totals ct CROSS JOIN stats s ORDER BY ct.total_spent DESC

results.test_name: ambiguous_temporal: How are we doing this quarter?...

metadata.expected_sql: SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month', order_date) AS month, COUNT(*) AS order_count, SUM(total) AS revenue FROM orders WHERE order_date >= DATE_TRUNC('quarter', CURRENT_DATE) GROUP BY DATE_TRUNC('month', order_date) ORDER BY month

results.test_name: ambiguous_comparison: What's our best product?...

metadata.expected_sql: SELECT p.name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_sold, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_revenue FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.id = oi.product_id GROUP BY p.name ORDER BY total_revenue DESC LIMIT 1

results.test_name: multi_step_reasoning: Which customers haven't ordered anything in t...

metadata.expected_sql: SELECT c.name, MAX(o.order_date) AS last_order FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.id, c.name HAVING MAX(o.order_date) < CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '6 months' AND MAX(o.order_date) >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '12 months'

results.test_name: implicit_calculation: Are sales trending up or down?...

metadata.expected_sql: WITH monthly AS (SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month', order_date) AS month, SUM(total) AS revenue FROM orders WHERE order_date >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '12 months' GROUP BY DATE_TRUNC('month', order_date)) SELECT month, revenue, revenue - LAG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY month) AS change, CASE WHEN revenue > LAG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY month) THEN 'Up' WHEN revenue < LAG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY month) THEN 'Down' ELSE 'Flat' END AS trend FROM monthly ORDER BY month

results.test_name: complex_business_logic: Find customers who consistently order every m...

metadata.expected_sql: WITH monthly_orders AS (SELECT customer_id, DATE_TRUNC('month', order_date) AS month FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id, DATE_TRUNC('month', order_date)), with_gaps AS (SELECT customer_id, month, month - (ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY month) * INTERVAL '1 month') AS grp FROM monthly_orders), streaks AS (SELECT customer_id, MIN(month) AS streak_start, MAX(month) AS streak_end, COUNT(*) AS streak_months FROM with_gaps GROUP BY customer_id, grp) SELECT c.name, s.streak_start, s.streak_end, s.streak_months FROM streaks s JOIN customers c ON s.customer_id = c.id WHERE s.streak_months >= 3 ORDER BY s.streak_months DESC
